title: Mexican Rice (Arroz Rojo)
description: Mexican Rice (Arroz Rojo) is a classic side dish made with toasted long-grain rice simmered in a flavorful tomato and stock base. Light, fluffy, and aromatic, it pairs beautifully with tacos, enchiladas, grilled meats, and many traditional Mexican dishes.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: Long-grain white rice (preferably extra-long, not parboiled) – 1 cup
Neutral oil (vegetable, canola, or rendered chicken fat for depth) – 2 tbsp
Medium white onion, finely chopped – 1 (about ½ cup)
Medium ripe tomato (or ½ cup tomato purée) – 1
Chicken stock (unsalted, or vegetable stock for vegetarian option) – 1½ cups
Kosher salt – ½ tsp (adjust to taste)
Whole serrano chiles – 1–2 (optional, for aroma & light heat, not chopped)
Frozen peas & carrots – ¼ cup (optional, traditional in many Mexican homes)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prep the Base
steps: In a blender, purée the tomato, onion, and garlic until smooth. Add a splash of stock if needed. You should have about 1 cup purée.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Toast the Rice
steps: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add rice and toast, stirring constantly, until golden and nutty (6–8 min). This step ensures a fluffy, non-sticky texture.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Build Flavor
steps: Stir in the tomato purée, letting it fry with the rice until it thickens and deepens in color (3–4 min).

instruction.title: Step 4 – Simmer
steps: Pour in the stock, add the serrano chiles (whole), and bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce to low heat, cover tightly, and cook for 18 minutes without lifting the lid.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Rest & Finish
steps: Turn off heat, leave covered, and let rest for 10 minutes to finish steaming.
Fluff gently with a fork, fold in peas & carrots if using, and garnish with cilantro.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve as a side dish with enchiladas, carne asada, mole, or roasted chicken.
For a fine-dining plating: mold rice into a ring mold or ramekin for elegant presentation, topped with micro-cilantro.

chefTips: Rice selection matters: Use long-grain rice, never short-grain. Rinse 2–3 times until water runs clear to remove excess starch.
Oil-toasting step is key: Creates separation of grains.
Stock vs. water: Always use a flavorful stock for depth, but ensure it's low sodium so salt can be controlled.
Whole chile infusion: Traditional in top kitchens for subtle heat & aroma. Remove before serving.
No peeking while cooking: Steam escapes and rice becomes uneven.
